newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt police arrest 39 for trouble over priest.
newsitem.headline: Egypt police arrest 39 for trouble over priest.

text.p: Egypt's Interior Ministry said on Friday it had arrested 39 people who allegedly started a fire outside the house of a priest in a northern province.

A ministry statement said the trouble occurred on Wednesday when a suspected member of the outlawed Moslem Brotherhood and two accomplices spread a rumour that priest Ishaq el-Soryani planned to take over land next to his house to build a church.
A group of people in Greiss hamlet in the province of Menoufiya gathered and set fire to some wood outside the priest's house, the ministry said.
Moslem militants have targeted Christians along with senior officials, policemen and occasionally tourists in their attempt to overthrow the government and set up a strict Islamist state.

The spiritual leader of the Moslem Brotherhood, Egypt's largest and most influential fundamentalist group, said in April Christians should pay a special tax to the government and should not hold senior positions in the army in case Egypt went to war with a Christian country.
His comments came on the heels of two bloody Moslem militant attacks in which the majority of victims were Christians.

Suspected militants massacred 10 young Christians in a church in southern Egypt in February and shot dead 13 people in a bloody rampage in a predominantly Christian hamlet also in the south a month later.
The government has portrayed the outlawed and influential Brotherhood as a front for the violent militant groups.
But the organisation, Egypt's largest political Islamic group, denies the charge, saying it wants to change Egypt into a strict Islamic state through legal means such as elections.
